dedupe_keys.name: san francisco planning public space and public life studies

description: San Francisco Planning runs public life surveys that observe how public spaces function: counts of pedestrians and cyclists and inventories of stationary activities and behaviours, used to judge whether spaces meet needs of comfort, safety and ease of pedestrian movement. The department explains that regular counts give a baseline for testing whether changes to the city increase walking and walkability, and that stationary activity surveys show when, where and why people use public spaces; the project page offers the reports it produced or commissioned and a map of study locations. Coverage: study sites in San Francisco. Access: free reports on the project page. Licence: none stated. Caveats: results are in reports, not a machine-readable table, methods follow the Gehl-style public life survey tradition, and survey dates differ by site. Simulation uses: calibrating pedestrian and stay-activity models for plazas and streets, and before-and-after evaluation of public realm projects. Related records: the Melbourne pedestrian counting system and the temporary pedestrianisation perception survey.
